description: Transform byte-at-a-time delimiter scanning into parallel bit-stream operations by transposing the input into bitplanes and computing structural character bitmasks (comma, quote, newline) across 64-byte chunks simultaneously. This is the foundational technique from simdjson adapted to CSV's simpler grammar, where each structural character class becomes a u64 bitmask that can be processed with population count, leading-zero, and carry-propagation operations.
mathematical_formalization: Given input block B[0..63], compute bitmasks: M_comma = OR_{i=0}^{63} (B[i] == ',') << i, M_quote = OR (B[i] == '"') << i, M_newline = OR (B[i] == '\n') << i. Field boundaries at positions: P = {p : bit p set in (M_comma | M_newline) & ~in_quoted_region}. Throughput model: T = (N / W) * C_simd where W = SIMD width in bytes, C_simd = cycles per SIMD classify op.
analogical_connections: simdjson's stage-1 structural indexing: JSON structural chars ({, }, [, ], :, ,) are analogous to CSV's (comma, quote, newline)
DNA sequence motif scanning: SIMD-based k-mer matching uses the same vectorized comparison + bitmask extraction pattern
Network packet classification: TCAM-style parallel field matching mirrors the parallel character classification approach
implementation_hypothesis: Use _mm256_cmpeq_epi8 (AVX2) or vceqq_u8 (NEON) to compare 32/16 bytes against each target character simultaneously, then _mm256_movemask_epi8 / vshrn to collapse byte-match results into a u32/u16 bitmask. Process 64 bytes per iteration by concatenating two 32-byte results. Use POPCNT and TZCNT to iterate set bits for field boundary extraction.
experiment_seed: Benchmark the raw structural character detection throughput (bytes/second) on a 1GB CSV file with varying field counts (5, 20, 100 fields) on both x86-64 (AVX2, AVX-512) and ARM64 (NEON). Compare against scalar byte-by-byte scanning. Target: >10GB/s structural detection on AVX-512.
